# Latin ligature defaults: unresolved rendering controls

Generated by tools/latin_ligature_defaults_fixture.py from the project's original
OpenType fixture. No corpus text, artwork, or font binaries are included.
Each file has twelve right-aligned Calibri 20 pt paragraphs, with kerning off:
three original strings under omitted, none, standard, and standardContextual
ligature settings. Only enableOpenTypeFeatures differs between files (0/1).

The reference application exported both exact source paths read-only, one page
each. reference.json retains source/PDF hashes and text origins. Regenerate
with tools/record_latin_ligature_defaults.py and the directory containing
ligature-defaults-word-0.pdf and ligature-defaults-word-1.pdf. PDFs remain local.

All modes have identical origins with OpenType disabled. With it enabled,
omitted and none still match. Standard and standardContextual narrow the three
strings by 1.08, 1.92, and 0.48 pt respectively (PDF positioning quantization
applies). Both packages pass the standard MCE schema view. That view does not
validate the removed w14 extension or prove fidelity.

A separate Edge Canvas probe of the installed Calibri face at 2048 px gives
1141 units for `ti` by default, versus 1156 with FontFace featureSettings
`"liga" 0, "clig" 0`. Separate-letter measurement also gives 1156. Disabling
calt additionally does not change these samples. The default browser behavior
therefore cannot stand in for the DOCX ligature setting.

At the time of capture these were pre-implementation controls. A full
implementation must resolve inherited run properties and compatibility settings, preserve
required complex-script shaping, and apply identical features to measurement,
painting and caret positioning. No font-specific width correction is justified.

MS-DOCX section 2.3.3 specifies that enableOpenTypeFeatures gates OpenType
features and defaults off:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/116847ff-9af6-45a7-a21f-0e0ff2eef41d
The observations establish a browser/reference mismatch, not a proved reference/spec
contradiction. See also the existing opentype-kerning diagnostic.

These controls use explicit OpenType flags and do not establish its omitted
default in every compatibility mode. Subsequent [application-default controls](../script-kerning-defaults/README.md)
record the reference application's mode-15 omitted-flag divergence and the ligature defaults used
when the entire `rPrDefault` category is absent. This fixture's present defaults
and explicit flags retain the behavior documented above.

The default/none correction is now implemented and covered by
`tests/ligatures.test.js` and `tests/browser/ligatures.spec.js`. The historical
observations above remain the independent reference. All sixteen enum values
are retained, but separate discretionary/historical/contextual-only selection
and liga/clig distinctions are still pending; non-none rendering retains the
previous Canvas default. This does not certify all OpenType features.
